name: happy
title: The happy path: signed out to a submittable expense report, driven by the in-page fallback agent.
purpose: H3's accept runs `node harness/drive.mjs --fallback --scenario happy`. This file is what `--scenario happy` names. It is READ, not merely opened: drive.mjs cross-checks `walk[].count` against MEMBERSHIP in src/page/tools/compile.js and fails on a mismatch. A scenario file whose only job was to exist would be a check that discovered nothing — the numbers below have to be able to be WRONG, or naming them proves nothing.

walk.label: signed in as the employee persona
draft created and open, no lines yet
one clean line — the submit door opens

countsAreCrossChecked: Against MEMBERSHIP[state].length in src/page/tools/compile.js, which tools/validate-contracts.mjs proves equal to erp/contracts/tool-surface.contract.md §1 in both directions. If the contract moves, this file fails loudly rather than asserting a stale 2->6->13->14 that every document still quotes.

steps.note: The signed-out surface has two tools: get_signin_status and the resident explain_missing_tool. This status answer tells the agent that expense-workflow tools are unavailable until sign-in.

Reads the signed-in scope. The project code used below is DISCOVERED from this answer, never typed — a project the scope marks CLOSED would be a blocking violation (PROJECT_INACTIVE) and would fail a later step for a reason unrelated to the walk.
S1 -> S3. A draft opens and the editing surface appears.

steps.argsFrom: project discovered from get_session_scope; amount kept under the policy cap in src/policy.js
steps.note: S3 -> S2. One clean line, so submit_expense_report joins the surface — the flip this scenario exists to show.
Read-only confirmation that the report is submittable. The walk STOPS here: H3's accept ends at 14 and submitting would move the surface to S4 (7 tools), which is a different node's assertion.

stepsAreAGuide: drive.mjs owns the walk's mechanics — signing in through the page's own affordance, discovering the project code, deriving the line amount from src/policy.js's LIMITS so a moved cap cannot silently stop producing the intended state. `steps` records the intended shape for a reader and for the in-page demo (src/page/fallback-agent.js `selfDrive` takes exactly this `[{tool,args}]` form). It is NOT a second copy of the driver: where the two could drift, `walk[].count` is what drive.mjs actually gates on.
honesty: This scenario runs with --disable-features=WebMCP, so document.modelContext does not exist and src/page/fallback-agent.js installs a shim in its place. Everything here is therefore driven by a SIMULATED agent, labelled as such in #agent-banner and with ' · simulated agent' on the environment banner. A green run of this scenario is evidence that the tool surface and its state machine work — it is NOT evidence that a real third-party agent drove them, and at the tool boundary the two are indistinguishable.
